IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered for tenant="nimbus-corp" (reserved pool alert)
Severity: P1 — reserved-pool-backpressure / sustained tail-latency
Alerts: RP-THROTTLE-9921, KVCACHE-EVICT-301
Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/reserved-pool-backpressure

PagerDuty: Sent page to on-call (Sam R). Escalation policy: oncall->sre-lead->eng-manager.

Sam R: acked and taking ownership. I'm seeing a large increase in queue depth on nimbus-reserved-01. 99p gen latency spiking, errors creeping up (~5xx). Paging @Jin W to pull GPU util, queue depth, and active connections from the tenant pool. OpsEmily FYI (customer success) so they can prep comms if needed.

Jin W: digging in. quick metrics snapshot:
- reserved pool total GPUs: 8 (nimbus-reserved-01..08)
- avg GPU util: 92% (sustained on 4 nodes)
- request queue length: 1200 -> 1800 over last 8m
- 5xx rate: 0.9% -> 3.7%
- kv-cache miss ratio for tenant nimbus-corp: 0.62 (was ~0.12 baseline)
- typical seq len distribution shows a burst of very long sequences (avg tokens/request ~ 6k for this tenant)

Sam R: that kv-cache miss + long sequences explains memory churn and backpressure. I'm going to: 1) enable temporary fallback routing for this tenant to the hosted small model variant, 2) scale reserved pool by +2 GPUs, 3) apply short client throttling rule. Attempting steps now.

Sam R: applying fallback route (CLI):
```bash
rwctl routing set --tenant nimbus-corp --policy fallback:model=gpt-small-quant --ttl 900
```

Sam R: scaling reserved pool: increasing replica count on autoscaler for nimbus-reserved by +2 (requested nodes will be live in ~70s).

Jin W: running quick probe logs from the inference runtime on nimbus-reserved-03:```text
[2026-03-14T01:24:11Z] WARN  runtime: request queued (queue_size=1450)
[2026-03-14T01:24:13Z] ERROR runtime: dispatch failed: kvcache_eviction
[2026-03-14T01:24:14Z] ERROR runtime: backpressure applied, returning 429 to upstream
```

Sam R: pushed a temporary rate-limit rule to reduce client burst:```json
{"tenant":"nimbus-corp","route":"generate","burst":20,"rate":5,"action":"429"}
```

OpsEmily: notified Nimbus CSM and asked for any known load changes. CSM replied: they started a large internal stress test 6m ago by mistake and are throttling their runner. Waiting on confirmation.

Jin W: new nodes are joining: nimbus-reserved-09 and -10 are online. GPU util dropped from 92% -> 68% on impacted nodes. Queue length dropping (1800 -> 420). 5xx rate decreasing to 0.8%. kv-cache miss ratio still elevated but trending down (0.62 -> 0.34).

Sam R: verifying inference correctness on fallback path: sampled outputs look acceptable for degraded mode. Switching traffic back to reserved pool gradually; keeping fallback for small requests.

Lee M: stepping in for the next part of the incident (Sam, thanks). I'll keep monitoring for 15m then hand back if stable. @Jin W can you keep an eye on cache rebuild and eviction patterns? Also please collect the kernel-level GPU OOM logs for postmortem.

Jin W: will capture logs and export KV cache heatmaps. Commands I'm running now:
```bash
# export recent runtime logs
rwlogs export --cluster nimbus-reserved --since 10m --filter "kvcache_eviction" > /tmp/nimbus_kvcache_evictions.log
# dump cache hit histogram
rwctl metrics get --tenant nimbus-corp --metric kvcache.hit_histogram > /tmp/kvcache_hist.json
```

Sam R: note for post-incident: consider adding per-tenant long-sequence protection (max tokens per request soft cap), and a safety queue that rejects extreme-length requests earlier. Also add an alert to catch kv-cache miss ratio > 0.4 for reserved pools.

OpsEmily: Nimbus CSM confirms they stopped the internal stress test. They want a short incident summary for the account. I'll draft and share.

Lee M: after scaling and throttles, error rate is back to baseline and latency acceptable. We'll keep fallback routing for 10 more minutes to avoid immediate re-surge. I'll close once we hit 30m of stable metrics.

IncidentBot: Incident 1976543210 -> status: mitigated. Monitoring window: 30m. Postmortem owner: Sam R. Followups: add long-seq protection (sam-r), alert tuning for kv-cache misses (jin-w), customer comms (ops-emily).

Sam R: handing back to Lee M in 5m for observability window. Leaving a short notes block in the incident doc.

Lee M: acknowledged. continuing to monitor. tagging this thread for postmortem artifacts. :white_check_mark:
